source: Hand-curated Nov 2026. Names and coordinates from Google Places; tags and notes editorial. Seasonal facts checked against NPS pages (Bryce shuttle runs early April to mid-October; guided rides April to Oct 31) and local reports as of Nov 10, 2026: verify with NPS (nps.gov/brca) before booking. distMi is approximate road miles from the Bryce Canyon Visitor Center.

items.name: Bryce Canyon Visitor Center
items.note: Start here for ranger programs, the park film and the current trail and road conditions.

items.name: Sunrise Point
items.note: First-light rim view; the Queen's Garden and Fairyland trails drop from here.

items.name: Sunset Point
items.note: Evening rim view and the head of the Navajo Loop; a paved rim path links it to Sunrise Point.

items.name: Inspiration Point
items.note: Three-tier overlook; the short climb to the upper level gives the widest view of the amphitheater.

items.name: Bryce Point
items.note: Highest viewpoint in the main amphitheater and the south end of the Rim Trail; parking fills up.

items.name: Navajo Loop & Queen's Garden Trails
items.note: The classic 3-mile combo into the hoodoos from Sunrise or Sunset Point, with a steep climb back. Sections close for ice or rockfall in winter; check NPS.

items.name: Peekaboo Loop
items.note: Roller-coaster loop through tunnels and windows; shared with horse rides, hiked clockwise (about 5.5 miles from Bryce Point with the Connecting Trail).

items.name: Fairyland Loop Trail & Tower Bridge
items.note: 8-mile loop with steady climbs and fewer people; Tower Bridge is a short side spur.

items.name: Fairyland Point
items.note: Quiet overlook at the north end with a short rim walk; starting point of the Fairyland Loop.

items.name: Guided horse or mule ride (Canyon Trail Rides)
items.note: NPS concessioner rides into the amphitheater: 2-hour ($75) and 3-hour ($100) outings; ages 7+ for the 2-hour ride, 10+ for the 3-hour. Meeting point near the Lodge.
items.seasonNote: Guided rides typically run April through October 31, weather permitting.

items.name: The Lodge at Bryce Canyon Restaurant
items.note: Historic lodge dining room with a quinoa bowl and trout; reviewers call vegetarian options limited but present.
items.seasonNote: Lodge dining is typically seasonal (spring to fall); verify before counting on it.

items.name: Natural Bridge
items.note: A red-rock arch visible from the road, one of several pullouts along the 18-mile Scenic Drive.

items.name: Farview Point
items.note: Wide southern panorama with a short walk to a higher viewpoint and restrooms at the lot.

items.name: Rainbow Point & Yovimpa Point
items.note: End of the road at ~9,100 ft, two views 80+ miles to Navajo Mountain; Bristlecone Loop starts here.
items.seasonNote: Snow can close the southern end of the Scenic Drive in winter; check NPS.

items.name: Mossy Cave Trail
items.note: Under-a-mile stream-side walk to a small waterfall and a shallow overhang, on SR-12 east of the park road; reviewers say there is no entrance gate.

items.name: Canyon Diner (Ruby's Inn)
items.note: Counter-service pizza, burgers and rice bowls; a garden pizza and cheese pizza are on the menu.

items.name: Ruby's Inn Cowboy's Buffet & Steak Room
items.note: Log-cabin dining room with a lunch/dinner buffet and a large salad bar; a vegetarian burger is on the menu.

items.name: The Pizza Place (Tropic)
items.note: Crisp-crust pizza and local beer in Tropic; build-your-own and margherita options.

items.name: Bryce Canyon Pines Restaurant
items.note: Roadside diner on SR-12 known for pie; salads and steamed sides if you skip the elk burger.

items.name: Kodachrome Basin State Park
items.note: Stone spires, Panorama Trail and Indian Cave, with showers and a small shop; paved road in.

items.name: Red Canyon & Thunder Mountain arches
items.note: Hand-cut road tunnels on Scenic Byway 12 with short hikes and a bike path in Dixie National Forest.

items.name: Red Canyon Visitor Center
items.note: Dixie National Forest visitor center with short trails behind it.
items.seasonNote: Google lists 10-3 hours now; may be seasonal.

items.name: Cowboy's Smokehouse Cafe
items.note: Barbecue, steaks and breakfast on Panguitch's main street.

items.name: The Flying Goat
items.note: Panguitch coffee and breakfast diner with a bakery counter.

items.name: Cedar Breaks National Monument (Point Supreme)
items.note: Red-rock amphitheater above 10,000 ft; about 56 road miles west of Bryce via Panguitch and UT-143.
items.seasonNote: UT-148 is closed by snow outside roughly late May to October.

items.name: Zion Canyon Scenic Drive (by shuttle)
items.note: Zion Canyon's famous 6-mile corridor, ridden by shuttle in season. Riverside Walk at Temple of Sinawava is the easy pick.
items.seasonNote: Shuttle schedule changes by season: 2026 service runs to Nov 28, pauses Nov 29 to Dec 25, resumes Dec 26 to Jan 2.

items.name: Canyon Overlook Trail (Zion)
items.note: 1-mile round trip just east of the Mount Carmel tunnel, the first Zion stop from Bryce. SR-9 reopened Oct 9, 2026 after a rockfall, with a temporary gravel stretch.

items.name: Checkerboard Mesa Viewpoint (Zion)
items.note: Roadside pullout on SR-9 near the East Entrance.

items.name: Best Friends Animal Sanctuary
items.note: Largest no-kill animal sanctuary in Angel Canyon, ~1.5 hours south of Bryce; free tours.

items.name: Coral Pink Sand Dunes State Park
items.note: Coral-colored dunes with sandboard rentals; national park passes are not accepted.

items.name: Peekaboo Canyon Wood Fired Kitchen
items.note: Kanab's all-vegetarian-and-vegan restaurant with wood-fired pizza. Closed Mondays.

items.name: Angel Village Cafe
items.note: Plant-based buffet lunch at Best Friends, 11:30 to 1 daily.

items.name: Rocking V Cafe
items.note: Art-filled eatery in an 1892 mercantile; meats to vegan plates.
